cliInstall.title: Setup guide
cliInstall.lead: Connect Codex or Claude Code to MIY. Use the guide to install the CLI yourself, look up commands or manage your connections.
cliInstall.oneLineLead: Paste the command below into a terminal on your PC. It downloads the installer, checks its hash and registers the server automatically.
cliInstall.unixNote: Picks your OS and CPU automatically. Installs into ~/.local/bin and adds it to your shell's PATH. Open a new terminal after installing.
cliInstall.unixMissing: No Linux·macOS CLI package has been published on this server yet. Ask the server administrator to publish one.
cliInstall.windowsNote: Run it in PowerShell on Windows x64. Installs for the current user without administrator rights and adds it to PATH.
cliInstall.windowsMissing: No Windows CLI package has been published on this server yet. Ask the server administrator to publish one.
cliInstall.guiServer: If you use the GUI installer, enter the server address below. On a PC installing for the first time, the server address field is empty.
cliInstall.updateStop: Stop the local preview and any agent using the CLI, then rerun the installer for your OS as the same user.
cliInstall.updateProjects: Check that it shows the version above, then run the new global CLI in each app project folder. Running the project's existing executable does not update it to the new version.
cliInstall.setupCommand: Update the project CLI and MCP
cliInstall.reopenAgents: Reopen Codex or Claude Code to load the MCP and guides again. If you see an error that the SDK bundle differs, review and commit your changes, then run miy app upgrade explicitly.
cliInstall.projectBinary: Check the version of the project executable (.miy-tools/miy, or .miy-tools/miy.exe on Windows) and auth status. Updating alone does not require signing in again. If credential store errors continue, you can report them without signing in with report send --message "credential store error" from the same executable.
cliInstall.loginRegisters: The command above registers this server address as a connection. The CLI has no default IP or domain. Your existing connections and credentials are kept.
cliInstall.httpWarning: This server uses an internal HTTP setup, so traffic is not encrypted.
cliInstall.loginWhen: Run this the first time you authenticate or when an error says you need to authenticate again. In the browser that opens, check the account and verification code, then approve the connection.
cliInstall.contextList: If you already have connections, check the server to sign in to with miy context list first.
cliInstall.agentGuide: Open the setup instructions for agents
cliInstall.agentIntro: Open the project folder for an existing MIY app, or the parent folder where you want to create a new one. Choose your agent and copy the request into its first message.
cliInstall.codexSteps: Run codex in a terminal in your working folder. MIY configures the MCP in .codex/config.toml and provides project instructions in AGENTS.md.
cliInstall.claudeSteps: Run claude in a terminal in your working folder. MIY configures the MCP in .mcp.json and provides project instructions in CLAUDE.md. Review the configuration when asked to approve the project MCP.
cliInstall.verifyAgent: If sign-in is needed, check the account and code in your browser and approve the connection yourself. After setup, reopen the agent in the app folder and ask it to call miy_app’s get_contract and show the SDK contract and platform bundle version. The returned platformBundleVersion confirms it reached the server.
cliInstall.signupLead: New to this platform? Request an account, then use the link from your administrator to set your password before signing in with the CLI.
cliInstall.agentConfirm: Approve sign-in and verify the connection
cliInstall.agentNext: If the tools are missing, check the project settings and working directory.
cliInstall.installCheckBody: Compare the version printed by the first command with the published version above. The second command should show the identity you approved.
cliInstall.usageContextBody: A context is a named connection to a server. From your working folder, check the selected address and signed-in account. With several servers, replace NAME in miy --context NAME auth status with the context name to check one explicitly.
cliInstall.usageExistingBody: Open the root of your MIY app checkout and run the installed CLI. It prepares the compatible project executable, agent instructions and MCP settings. Continue with project checks if you already have an app.
cliInstall.usageNewBody: For a new app, run this from the parent folder. Replace the example path, app ID and display name with your own. Run the remaining commands inside the generated folder.
cliInstall.usageCheckBody: Sync shared components and check the managed files and app integration rules. The final diagnostic checks the project MCP and development tools. Follow the details for any failed check, then rerun it.
cliInstall.usagePreview: Start and stop a local preview
cliInstall.usagePreviewBody: From the app root, use an account with development access. Open the preview URL printed by the CLI. When finished, run miy app dev-stop in the same folder to stop the development processes.
cliInstall.usageRelease: Inspect the server build and release workflow
cliInstall.usageReleaseBody: For a registered app, inspect its deployment status. Server builds start from a clean, committed checkout. Use app deploy for dev, app accept to record acceptance and app promote for an accepted release. Inspect each command’s target and permissions before running it.
cliInstall.refIntro: Open docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md in the generated app for the workflow and full reference matching its CLI version. Use the commands below for a narrower lookup. Agent instructions start in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md.
cliInstall.refHelp: List command groups and app subcommands
cliInstall.refApi: App API contracts and OpenAPI workflow
cliInstall.refMachine: Read the current context as JSON for automation
cliInstall.mcpIntro: For app development, use the project’s miy_app server. The agent starts the project CLI as a local process and calls its tools over standard input and output (stdio). This server uses your CLI context and sign-in.
cliInstall.mcpLocalBody: For an existing app or a fresh checkout, run the installed CLI in the app root. It generates settings for this machine and prepares .miy-tools/miy (.miy-tools/miy.exe on Windows). The generated launch argument is mcp.
cliInstall.mcpNew: Creating a new app also generates its MCP settings.
cliInstall.mcpCodexBody: Run this in the project root to inspect the entry from .codex/config.toml. Open the trusted project in a new Codex session and enter /mcp to inspect its tools.
cliInstall.mcpClaudeBody: Review .mcp.json in the app folder and approve the project MCP when prompted in Claude Code. Inspect the entry with this command and use /mcp in a new session to check the connection.
cliInstall.mcpTools: 3. Call the tools from the agent
cliInstall.mcpToolsBody: Ask the agent to call both tools on miy_app. The first returns local API guidance without signing in. The second verifies the project bundle and returns the platformBundleVersion read from the server.
cliInstall.mcpRemote: Connect an external MCP client over HTTP
cliInstall.mcpRemoteBody: To use platform tools outside the project, add a Streamable HTTP connection in your client and enter this server URL. Use the OAuth client ID and redirect URI registered for that client by your administrator, then authenticate in the browser.
cliInstall.mcpRemoteVerify: After connecting, call the remote get_cli_update_guide tool and check the portal installation URL. This connection has its own OAuth session. If it expires, sign in again from that MCP client.
cliInstall.manageSessionsBody: Inspect the sessions for your devices. To end the current session, run miy auth logout. To revoke another, match its device and session ID, then replace ID in miy auth sessions revoke ID. You can also manage your sessions in the console.
cliInstall.manageSessionsLink: Open my CLI connections in the console
cliInstall.manageLogin: When the CLI is installed but authentication fails
cliInstall.manageLoginBody: Compare the current context with the server address shown in this guide. Check the identity and server diagnostics. If approval expired or the session was revoked, run miy auth login in that context and approve the new request in your browser.
cliInstall.manageTools: When the CLI works but agent tools are missing
cliInstall.manageToolsBody: Run diagnostics from the app root. For stale paths or MCP settings, run the global miy app setup there and reopen the agent. Once the local checks pass, call get_contract as described in MCP setup to verify server access.
cliInstall.refLookup: Look up details for your installed version
cliInstall.refList: List the apps visible to your signed-in account.
cliInstall.refRegister: From the app root, submit the app for administrator approval.
cliInstall.refCheck: Run local checks for project integration, Rust tests and the frontend.
cliInstall.refBuild: Submit the committed app source to the server for checks and a release build.
cliInstall.refDryRun: Preview the target and proposed changes before deploying to dev.
cliInstall.refStatus: Inspect the current app’s server deployment state.
